title: On Returning the borrowed tools on the same day
subtitle: 交通出行 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 交通出行（人与自我·生活与学习·出行与交通）
meta: 主题语境：交通出行（人与自我·生活与学习·出行与交通）　|　核心词汇：return　|　正文 362 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 return 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1956 the cook ① returned the borrowed tools on the same day in silence, and every guest in the canteen said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three days on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the cook ② returns the borrowed tools on the same day twice over without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ return the borrowed tools on the same day at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ returned the borrowed tools on the same day before — a line in the menu for September 1950 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Returning the borrowed tools on the same day in silence, the cook said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the bowl at the far table, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ return to the valley after forty years twice over, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Return to the valley after forty years at once and never mention it again.

By 1963 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the menu, and a new guest from the next canteen ⑧ returns to the valley after forty years in silence every day without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the table, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ returned the borrowed tools on the same day again when nobody else would.

⑩ To return the borrowed tools on the same day, my mother said in 1968, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the canteen remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the canteen forgets, somebody returns the borrowed tools on the same day twice over again and somebody must return the borrowed tools on the same day in silence all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 归还（一般过去式 returned the borrowed tools on the same day：1956 年厨子头一回这样做，一言不发地）
B. v. 归还（一般现在 returns the borrowed tools on the same day：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 归还（不定式 to return the borrowed tools on the same day：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 归还（过去完成时 had returned the borrowed tools on the same day：1950 年九月的菜单上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 归还（动名词 returning the borrowed tools on the same day 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 返回（return to the valley after forty years：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去返回四十年后回到那条山谷）
G. v. 返回（return to the valley after forty years：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 归还（后段两处：新来的客人照例 returns to the valley after forty years，而母亲又一次 returned the borrowed tools on the same day）

answers.why: return 意为“归还”，1956 年厨子一言不发地归还当天就把借来的工具还了，那是食堂里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 returned。
return 意为“归还”，自那以后厨子来回两遍把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 returns。
return 意为“归还”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯归还当天就把借来的工具还了”，此处为不定式 to return the borrowed tools on the same day。
return 意为“归还”，菜单里 九月 那行字说明早在 1963 年之前就有人归还过，故用过去完成时 had returned。
return 意为“归还”，厨子说“归还当天就把借来的工具还了这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 returning the borrowed tools on the same day 作主语。
return 意为“返回”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去返回四十年后回到那条山谷”，should ever 之后用原形 return to the valley after forty years。
return 意为“返回”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻返回四十年后回到那条山谷（return to the valley after forty years at once），以后再也不要提起。
return 意为“归还”，新来的客人每个日子都照例返回四十年后回到那条山谷，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 returns。
return 意为“归还”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次一言不发地归还当天就把借来的工具还了，用一般过去式 returned 叙述。
return 意为“归还”，结尾那句是母亲 1968 年的话：要归还当天就把借来的工具还了，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和食堂记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 return 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1956 the cook returned the borrowed tools on the same day in silence, and nobody in the canteen forgot it.
Even now the cook returns the borrowed tools on the same day twice over whenever the canteen asks.
Returning the borrowed tools on the same day in silence, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever return to the valley after forty years twice over, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new guest from the next canteen returns to the valley after forty years in silence every day, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother returned the borrowed tools on the same day again, and the canteen remembered that half.
